questions.q: Which filter defines the case backlog?
options: Closed equals True
Priority equals Low
Closed equals False
Origin equals Email
questions.explain: The backlog is the set of cases that are not closed, so filter Closed equals False.

questions.q: Why add a maximum or age buckets next to an average resolution time?
options: Because averages cannot be calculated on cases
Because an average can hide a long tail of very old cases
Because buckets are required by dashboards
Because maximums are always equal to averages
questions.explain: Nine fast cases and one very slow one give a small average that hides an unhappy customer. Maximums and buckets expose the tail.

questions.q: Why is it hard to show cases opened and cases closed in one ordinary summary report?
options: Cases cannot be grouped by date
Only closed cases can be reported on
Reports cannot show two lines
They depend on two different date fields, so each needs its own grouping
questions.explain: Opened and closed dates are different fields. Use two reports side by side, or a joined report with two blocks.

questions.q: What is a known limitation of relying on a joined report for an opened versus closed dashboard?
options: Joined reports are limited for charting and dashboard use, so two separate reports are often more practical
Joined reports cannot include dates
Joined reports only work on leads
Joined reports delete case data
questions.explain: Joined reports have restrictions when it comes to charts and dashboard components, which is why the two-report approach is common.

questions.q: What is true about native case age fields?
options: They automatically exclude weekends and holidays
They measure customer satisfaction
They are only available on closed cases
They are calendar time, so business-hours aging needs Entitlements or a custom calculation
questions.explain: Native age is elapsed calendar time. Business-hours measurement requires more setup.
